title: Struggling with cover animations and weapon hand placement in Unreal Engine 5.9. Any advice?
author: Faisal_alwaal
selftext:
​

Hey everyone,

I'm working on a third-person shooter in Unreal Engine 5.9, and I've been struggling quite a bit with animations, especially the cover system and how the character holds weapons like rifles and shotguns.

The hand placement always looks off. The hands don't line up properly, and the whole thing just looks awkward.

I'm also having trouble with the cover system. I want the character to move naturally when entering cover, leaning out, aiming, and switching sides, but I just can't seem to get the animations to look right.

I've tried generating animations with Kimodo, but the results haven't been great either.

I'm honestly starting to think I should just buy an animation pack or a complete cover system from Fab, but I'd rather learn how to do it myself if possible.

Has anyone here run into the same issues? How did you solve them? Is there a specific workflow or tool you guys use for this kind of stuff?

I'm still learning Unreal, so I'd really appreciate any advice or suggestions

comments.author: VortexAssetStudio
comments.body: For the weapon hand placement, you don't actually need to regenerate the animations. Look into using Two-Bone IK (Inverse Kinematics) in your Animation Blueprint. You can attach a socket to the weapon's foregrip and force the left hand to snap to it dynamically, which fixes the alignment issue completely. As for the cover system, blending entry, leaning, and side-switching from scratch is one of the toughest parts of a TPS. Honestly, grabbing a solid template from Fab just to study how they structure the state machines might save you weeks of frustration!

replies.author: Faisal_alwaal
replies.body: Thank you so much, i will try that

replies.author: VortexAssetStudio
replies.body: No problem at all, good luck with the build!
